title: Simulating generic single-qubit open-dynamics via polarization-frequency coupling in a photonic interferometer
authors: Kalle Raikisto, Alberto Ferrara, Tom Kuusela, Rosario Lo Franco, Jyrki Piilo
abstract: We propose a photonic platform for simulating arbitrary single-qubit open-system dynamics using a single photon in an open Mach-Zehnder interferometer. A birefringent quartz plate induces a coupling between the polarization and frequency degrees of freedom. By treating the latter as an effective environment, we analytically derive the reduced polarization dynamics. We show that the resulting evolution is characterized by a controllable interplay between populations and coherence, instead of the usual dephasing caused by quartz plates. By adjusting the photon frequency distribution and interferometric parameters, we demonstrate that target single-qubit states can be efficiently reproduced through a tunable optical protocol expected to work under accessible experimental conditions. The simulator is benchmarked against paradigmatic open-system evolutions, including depolarization and non-Markovian dynamics, achieving high accuracy. Our results establish polarization-frequency engineered photonic interferometers as a versatile protocol for simulation of open quantum systems.
summary: The authors propose using a photonic interferometer with birefringent quartz to simulate arbitrary single-qubit open dynamics. By treating the photon's frequency as an effective environment, they derive a controllable mechanism that allows simulating non-Markovian and general decoherence processes. This establishes polarization-frequency engineered interferometers as a versatile tool for quantum simulation.
main_problem: The goal is to simulate arbitrary single-qubit open-system dynamics using a controllable photonic platform.
main_result: The setup successfully simulates general qubit decoherence, including non-Markovian effects like coherence revivals, by engineering the coupling between polarization and frequency degrees of freedom.
method: The simulation involves analyzing the partial trace over the continuous frequency environment degree of freedom after a photon passes through a birefringent quartz plate within an interferometer.
model_or_system: The physical system is a single photon in an open Mach-Zehnder interferometer containing a birefringent quartz plate. The qubit dynamics are governed by coupling polarization (the system) to the frequency spectrum (the environment).
key_observables: Reduced density matrix elements ($ho_{00}, ho_{01}$), mean fidelity, and output photon probabilities ($p_j$).
important_parameters: Frequency distribution parameters ($\mu, \sigma$), quartz plate thickness ($\ell$), initial populations, and relative phase ($\phi$).
main_assumptions: The frequency environment is modeled using a Gaussian distribution, and the analysis relies on partial tracing over this continuous spectrum.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup (MZI with quartz), show probability distributions vs. $\mu$ or $\sigma$, and compare simulated qubit evolution (e.g., amplitude damping) against theoretical benchmarks like depolarization channels.
paper_structure: The paper details the derivation of the output state by tracing out frequency, derives measurable quantities ($\eta_\lambda, \kappa_A$), and then applies this formalism to benchmark simulations for various open dynamics regimes (depolarizing, non-Markovian).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally accessible optical protocol—'optical reservoir engineering'—to simulate complex quantum dissipation channels beyond simple Markovian decay.
